api-reference/overview.title: API Overview
api-reference/overview.description: The Django API is namespaced under:

architecture/backend.title: Backend
architecture/backend.description: The backend is Django REST Framework with Celery-based asynchronous operations.

architecture/confidential-engine.title: Confidential Engine
architecture/confidential-engine.description: The confidential engine is the private execution layer that allows Balary to move sensitive computation away from public execution while preserving verifiable blockchain coordination.

architecture/contracts.title: Contracts
architecture/contracts.description: The current Balary application uses the confidential payroll contract pair:

architecture/frontend.title: Frontend
architecture/frontend.description: The Balary frontend is a React + TypeScript + Vite application using Viem for wallet interaction.

architecture/lifecycle-controller.title: Lifecycle Controller
architecture/lifecycle-controller.description: Balary's V2 lifecycle controller exists because confidential-compute identity is operational state that can change across TEE restarts.

architecture/overview.title: Architecture Overview
architecture/overview.description: Balary separates private computation from public verification and settlement.

deployment/backend-fcc.title: Backend and FCC
deployment/backend-fcc.description: The live Balary stack places Django, Celery, Redis, the FCC proxy, simulated hackathon TEE and lifecycle controller behind server-controlled configuration.

deployment/coston2.title: Coston2
deployment/coston2.description: Balary currently runs on Flare Testnet Coston2.

deployment/frontend.title: Frontend
deployment/frontend.description: The frontend is a Vite application and is deployed on Vercel for the current Balary project.

employee/overview.title: Employee Overview
employee/overview.description: An employee uses the wallet stored on their employee record to authenticate and access only the payroll/claim data permitted for that identity.

employee/private-withdrawals.title: Private Withdrawals
employee/private-withdrawals.description: This page describes the current core-payroll withdrawal API.

employer/confidential-compute.title: Request Confidential Computation
employer/confidential-compute.description: Once the payroll is encrypted, HR moves the run onto Coston2 and then asks FCC to process the confidential payroll.

employer/create-payroll.title: Create a Payroll
employer/create-payroll.description: HR creates a payroll run in Django before any payroll-specific transaction is signed.

employer/fund-and-activate.title: Fund and Activate
employer/fund-and-activate.description: Funding is intentionally separated from confidential computation.

employer/overview.title: Employer Overview
employer/overview.description: Employer operations are split between Admin, HR and Finance rather than giving one wallet every capability.

employer/schedules-and-audit.title: Schedules and Audit
employer/schedules-and-audit.description: Balary's operational backend includes recurring schedule shells, notifications and audit reports in addition to the on-chain payroll lifecycle.

fcc-integration/instruction-flow.title: Instruction Flow
fcc-integration/instruction-flow.description: The confidential compute path is intentionally multi-stage so that a browser transaction alone cannot manufacture a trusted payroll result.

fcc-integration/overview.title: FCC Overview
fcc-integration/overview.description: Balary is designed around the core Confidential Compute principle: private execution with public verification.

fcc-integration/tee-lifecycle.title: TEE Lifecycle
fcc-integration/tee-lifecycle.description: TEE lifecycle management is part of Balary's security boundary, not just deployment plumbing.

getting-started.title: Getting Started
getting-started.description: This guide gets a developer oriented around the current Balary stack. The app is a multi-service system, so start by understanding the boundaries before running individual components.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.description: Balary is a confidential payroll computation application powered by Flare Confidential Compute.

product-overview/user-journeys.title: User Journeys
product-overview/user-journeys.description: Balary separates institution administration, HR preparation, Finance funding and employee settlement.

product-overview/what-is-balary.title: What is Balary?
product-overview/what-is-balary.description: Balary is a Flare Confidential Compute application that uses payroll as a real-world demonstration of private off-chain execution connected to verifiable on-chain workflows.

product-overview/why-confidential-payrol.title: Why Confidential Payroll?
product-overview/why-confidential-payrol.description: Balary demonstrates why Confidential Compute matters: sensitive inputs can remain private while blockchain systems still receive usable, verifiable results.

security/permissions.title: Permissions
security/permissions.description: Balary combines off-chain role checks with on-chain contract roles.

security/privacy-model.title: Privacy Model
security/privacy-model.description: Balary's privacy model protects payroll computation and private authorization state, not every visible blockchain artifact.

verification/deployed-contracts.title: Deployed Contracts
verification/deployed-contracts.description: This page records the current Balary Coston2 deployment used by the live hackathon application.

verification/test-evidence.title: Test Evidence
verification/test-evidence.description: The V2 source snapshot records a broad validation pass across the stack.
